validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE CONFIRMED, independent of the sheet's own citations. This is the Uzhhorod area branch that feeds the real, active Ukraine-Hungary cross-border gas interconnector at Berehove (Ukrainian-side interconnection point name 'IP Beregovo') / Beregdaróc, Hungary (Hungarian-side 'IP Beregdaróc'). History: an 800mm tap off the Dolyna-Uzhhorod-border ('Bratstvo') system opened 1975, superseded/supplemented in 1986 by a 1400mm connector off the Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod ('Soyuz') system; the 1975 800mm line was reactivated in 2013 for reverse-flow imports into Ukraine. In May 2020 Gas TSO of Ukraine (GTSOU) and Hungary's FGSZ merged the two physical points into a single 'VIP Bereg' virtual interconnection point (joint FGSZ/GTSOU business-rules notice, verified live). A named 'Ужгород-Берегово (Берегово)' line also appears independently in a third-party Ukraine gas-transit capacity table (eegas.com), which traces to Gazprom/Naftogaz transit data, not to GEM. So this is NOT a GEM-only/hallucinated entity. CAVEAT: none of the FOUR citations already on the gem.wiki page actually establish this — the tsoua.com 'key facts' and LinkedIn refs are generic GTSOU-identity pages (say nothing about this specific line), and teplogidromash.ru's 'ЭКСПОРТ СИЯНИЕ СЕВЕРА' is about the much larger Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod trunk (P0768), not about a Berehove branch. Only the eegas.com ref actually names this route, and even that one gives a capacity figure that conflicts with the sheet (see spec concern). The real support for this row's existence came from fresh independent research (Ukrainian Wikipedia + the FGSZ VIP Bereg notice), not from the wiki's own footnotes — a good reminder that a wiki page can cite real, live pages that nonetheless don't actually support the specific claim.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet (and gem.wiki, which frames it as the pipeline 'redistributing' gas 'within Ukraine') presents this purely as a domestic Ukrainian line. Independent sourcing shows it is actually the Ukraine side of an active international gas interconnector to Beregdaróc, Hungary — unified in 2020 into a joint GTSOU/FGSZ 'VIP Bereg' virtual point with bidirectional booked capacity (export UA->HU and import HU->UA). That is a materially different characterization than 'redistribution within Ukraine.' Recording StartLocation=Uzhgorod/EndLocation=Berehove (both Ukraine) is defensible AS FAR AS IT GOES if the row is meant to represent only the Ukrainian-side segment terminating at the border (matching the interconnection point's Ukrainian name 'IP Beregovo'), but the missing cross-border context is a real gap, not a nitpick — a reader of the sheet would not know this line has anything to do with Hungary. Separately, the two wiki-family sources disagree on provenance: gem.wiki says gas arrives via the Dolyna-Uzhhorod pipeline (17 bcm/y); Ukrainian Wikipedia's Berehove-Beregdaróc article says the currently active 1400mm connector was built in 1986 off the Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhhorod trunk specifically (with the original 1975 800mm Dolyna-Uzhhorod-fed line kept as a separate, later-reactivated reverse-flow line). These aren't necessarily irreconcilable (both trunks converge in the Uzhhorod area) but the sheet's StartLocation='Uzhgorod' quietly papers over a real ambiguity about which trunk this branch taps.

validity.recommendation: Do not treat 13.00 bcm/y as settled. Have a researcher reconcile against GTSOU/FGSZ's currently published entry-exit capacities (ENTSOG Transparency Platform is the cleanest live source) rather than banking the wiki figure.
validity.researcher_notes: Capacity = 13.00 bcm/y on the sheet cannot be corroborated by two agreeing independent sources — every source I could verify gives a DIFFERENT number: (1) eegas.com's Ukraine transit-capacity table (the only wiki-cited source that actually names this route) lists 'Ужгород-Берегово (Берегово)' at 11 bcm/y across 2 pipes — an 18% gap from the sheet, material by the >=2-independent-agreement standard; (2) Ukrainian Wikipedia's Berehove-Beregdaróc article gives 'up to 13 billion m3/year' but explicitly as the design/theoretical capacity of the 1986 1400mm connector alone, not a measured/contracted figure, and its date is unclear; (3) the FGSZ/GTSOU 'VIP Bereg' joint notice (2020, primary regulatory document, verified live) states current allocatable technical capacity as UA->HU firm 1,895,054 m3/h (~16.6 bcm/y annualized) plus interruptible 1,686,576 m3/h, and HU->UA firm 0 / interruptible up to 3,581,630 m3/h (~31 bcm/y annualized, matching the ~975 GWh/d figure Argus Media reported for the same May-2020 capacity rise). None of these three numbers agree with each other or with the sheet's 13.00, and they aren't obviously reconcilable as the same measurement (nameplate vs. table vs. current firm+interruptible booking capacity, one-way vs. bidirectional). I did not find two sources that independently AGREE on 13.00, so I am not proposing a ref for the existing value, and I am not substituting a different number myself (no single figure here is clearly 'the' answer to the same question the sheet is asking). Flagging as a genuine material spec conflict per the corroboration rule.

fills.researcher_notes: Status is inferable from context, not a literal keyword match. FGSZ's 2020 'VIP Bereg' notice describes live bidirectional capacity allocation and auctions at this exact interconnection point (present-tense, ongoing regulatory arrangement); Ukrainian Wikipedia describes the 2013 reverse-flow reactivation and ongoing use through at least 2016; both independently confirm the asset is in active service, not idle/decommissioned.
Both sources are explicitly about a natural-gas transmission interconnection point (VIP/IP entry-exit capacity in m3/h and kWh/h of natural gas).

Confirms EndLocation=Berehove, Ukraine specifically as a real, named interconnection point ('IP Beregovo') on the Ukrainian gas transmission system, on the border with Hungary at Beregdaróc. StartLocation=Uzhgorod is supported only as the general area/hub the feeder trunk passes through (see the classification concern above for the unresolved ambiguity about which specific upstream trunk feeds this branch) — cite this ref for the Berehove end with more confidence than the Uzhgorod origin.

Diameter was blank on the sheet — deep-filled. FGSZ's 2020 VIP Bereg notice names the two physical interconnection entry-exit points explicitly as 'Beregdaróc 1400 UA->HU' and 'Beregdaróc 800 HU->UA' (DN in mm). Independently, Ukrainian Wikipedia's Berehove-Beregdaróc history gives the same two figures: the original 1975 line was 800mm, and the 1986 addition (still the primary export-direction line) was 1400mm; the 800mm line was reactivated (not replaced) in 2013 for reverse flow. Two parallel physical lines of different diameter exist at this crossing today, hence the multi-value format used elsewhere in the roster (e.g. P0768's '1420, 1400'). PDF url_verifier check came back 'ok but contains_value:false' on a straight substring test (the extractor did not surface '1400 UA>HU' cleanly) — confirmed manually via pdftotext -layout on the fetched PDF, which shows the figures verbatim.

See the spec concern in validity[] — three checkable sources give three different capacity figures (11 bcm/y, 'up to 13' bcm/y design, and ~16.6/~31 bcm/y directional technical from the 2020 VIP Bereg allocation), none of which independently corroborate the sheet's 13.00 to the required 2-agreeing-source standard. Left UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate agreement or silently pass a conflicting number.

That page is GTSOU's own self-description as Ukraine's post-2020 gas TSO — a primary/self-declared source, paired with the independent FGSZ document, which specifically names 'Gas TSO of Ukraine LLC (UA TSO)' as the entry/exit TSO for THIS exact interconnection point (VIP Bereg), not just as Ukraine's TSO in general. Only the Ukrainian-side 100% is being confirmed here — the Hungarian-side infrastructure at the same interconnection is FGSZ's, per the same document; since this GEM row's endpoints are both recorded in Ukraine, 100% GTSOU for the row as scoped is consistent, but see the classification concern about the row omitting the cross-border half of the picture entirely.

summary: P0780 is a real, active Ukraine-Hungary gas interconnector (Berehove/'IP Beregovo' <-> Beregdaróc, Hungary, unified into GTSOU/FGSZ's 'VIP Bereg' since 2020) mischaracterized on gem.wiki as purely domestic 'redistribution' -- flagged classification concern; capacity 13.00 bcm/y conflicts with every independently checkable source (11 / 'up to 13' design / ~16.6-31 technical) -- flagged spec concern, left UNRESOLVED; not a duplicate of P1489/P3063 (different border crossing).
